A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIX-HIC, with matching core architecture, datasets, and downstream tasks. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite v2's reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, few-shot and cross-cell evaluations, modality ablations, and appendix analyses of loop validation and hyperparameters.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds loss ablations, feature measurements, epigenomic perturbation experiments, and noise-robustness results.

M1.justification: The encoders, cross-modal interaction and mapping blocks, fusion mechanism, task decoders, and training objectives remain unchanged. Renaming InferMap to Infer and evaluating additional uses of the existing bidirectional mapping do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The four pre-training cell lines, GM12878/K562 evaluation datasets, and three downstream tasks remain. v2 removes cross-cell Hi-C-map prediction and adds loop-detection scenarios with attenuated epigenomic signals and noisy/sparse Hi-C inputs (Appendices C.5–C.6), changing test coverage within the existing domain.

E2.justification: Peakachu is added to the few-shot comparison in Figure 4, alongside the existing non-pretrained MIX-HIC and DLoopCaller comparisons. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables remains unchanged; Appendix D mostly expands descriptions of already evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain R2 but drop PCC, while regression ablations switch from PCC to R2. New protocols include staged loss removal, signal attenuation at 118 CTCF-anchored loops, and corruption of nonzero Hi-C contacts. Existing chromosome splits, sample counts, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds loss-specific ablations (Table 5), evaluates epigenomic-feature completion from Hi-C (Table 6), and introduces feature-diversity, biological-perturbation, and noise-robustness analyses (C.4–C.6). It quantifies the existing chromosome-13 case study but removes cross-cell Hi-C-map analysis. The original hyperparameter experiments remain as Figures 7–8.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports feature inner products with accompanying ± quantities, extending uncertainty reporting beyond the existing few-shot plots. Their meaning and replication counts are unspecified. Figure 4 retains five independent seeded runs and standard errors; no increase in replication is documented.

E6.justification: MIX-HIC's main benchmark scores remain unchanged, but several comparator scores change: DLoopCaller GM12878 AUROC falls from 0.9118 to 0.9046, Peakachu K562 recall from 0.8062 to 0.7905 (Table 3), and EPCOT-LSTM K562 CAGE R2 from 0.8972 to 0.8704 (Table 4). These revisions alter margins and make MIX-HIC lead every Table 3 metric. Loop counts and some cross-cell/ablation values also change. Main PCC and cross-cell-map results disappear, while substantial new ablation, perturbation, and robustness results appear.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 in v2 Section 4.1 restates v1 Appendix B's information-gap bound with the same perfect-alignment assumption and proof. Equation splitting, renumbering, and explaining the existing validation-proportion metric introduce no substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the first multimodal 3D-genome foundation model, two cross-modal blocks, a dataset exceeding one million pairs, and state-of-the-art performance on three tasks across two evaluation cell lines.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of few-shot data efficiency, feature diversity, and moderate model sizes, and interprets perturbation and noise results as evidence of biological grounding and robust representations. New Appendix E discusses missing DNA-sequence integration, bulk-sequencing applicability versus single-cell analysis, and limited pre-training cell-line diversity.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code/dataset release; v2 reports code availability and supplies a repository address. v2 also documents CAGE-seq normalization, Hi-C/CAGE log transformations, FIMO motif identification, and software/license information. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish changes to the retained preprocessing procedures or core hyperparameters.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references on medical-imaging and protein foundation models, sequencing biases, Hi-C noise, motif scanning, and HyenaDNA, and expands baseline descriptions in Appendix D. The central novelty positioning against task-specific genomics methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the exposition remain intact. v2 edits language, expands biological explanations, standardizes variant and task names, moves the theorem statement into the main text, and rewrites the few-shot and ablation discussions. Baseline, limitations, and checklist sections are appended.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout with extensively resized and relocated displays. The original ablation Figure 6 becomes Table 6; benchmark tables lose PCC columns and gain improvement annotations. Figure 5 loses map-prediction panels, Figure 4 gains a comparator curve, and the loop case study adds unmatched-interaction markers and proportions. Several new tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens component-level validation through direct loss ablations and feature measurements, adds informative perturbation/noise tests, and improves code-access and limitation disclosures. These provide a limited net quality improvement. The gain is constrained by removal of cross-cell Hi-C-map evidence and unexplained revisions to comparator scores; the unchanged main MIX-HIC results do not establish improved model performance.
